sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a North Bergen house?
sections.html:
A North Bergen owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an as-is purchase, and the best fit depends on tenants, a hillside lot and any open code issues. The township covers 5.14 square miles of land, QuickFacts estimates 61,483 residents, and that is 3.0% fewer than its 2020 base. Roughly 41.6% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, with a typical value of $473,500.

Before you choose, assemble what a buyer's attorney and the title company will ask for.

  • The deed and your latest tax bill.
  • Any certificate of occupancy for the building and its legal unit count.
  • Rent control registration if any unit is rented.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers for each tenant.

sections.h2: What is the land like in North Bergen?
sections.html:
The township is shaped like an inverted L. A northern arm runs east to west, and a southern arm runs north to south between Secaucus and the Hudson-side towns of Guttenberg, West New York and Union City. The Hudson River forms the eastern border, facing Manhattan, and the Hackensack River separates the township from Carlstadt. The Palisades rise from the waterfront, and a steep slope on the west side drops toward the Meadowlands.

That slope makes North Bergen the city with the second most hills per square mile in the United States, after San Francisco. Steep driveways, retaining walls and stairs up to the front door are features a buyer will want to inspect, so photograph and describe them honestly.

Low-lying ground on the west side is part of the New Jersey Meadowlands, so ask your insurance agent whether your parcel sits in a flood zone before you quote a closing date.

sections.h2: Which North Bergen neighborhoods belong in a listing?
sections.html:
Name the section, since housing type and transit access vary across the township.

  • Bergenline Avenue, a commercial strip with more than 300 stores and restaurants.
  • The Racetrack section, on the plateau between Bergenline Avenue and Kennedy Boulevard.
  • Bergenwood, clinging to the west-facing slope of the Palisades.
  • New Durham, near the Bergen Turnpike and Tonnelle Avenue.
  • Meadowview behind the Municipal Building, and Babbitt out in the Meadowlands.
  • Bulls Ferry and Woodcliff, toward the Hudson and North Hudson Park.

The Hackensack band of the Lenape lived here until the Dutch repurchased the land in 1658, and the township was incorporated on April 10, 1843. Spanish speakers began arriving in the 1960s, giving rise to the nickname Havana on the Hudson. Today 71.4% of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 74.5% of residents age 5 and up speak another language at home, so Spanish-language listings can reach a large share of local buyers.

sections.h2: How do transit and schools affect North Bergen sales?
sections.html:
Commuters buy here for buses and light rail. Route 495 links the Lincoln Tunnel with the Turnpike, and NJ Transit lines such as the 121, 125, 127 and 128 end at the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown. Jitneys on Bergenline Avenue can run as often as one a minute. The Hudson-Bergen Light Rail stops at Tonnelle Avenue and reaches Weehawken, Hoboken, Jersey City and Bayonne.

Residents take 33.1 minutes on average to reach work, so a block near a bus line or a light rail stop is worth highlighting. The North Bergen School District teaches pre-kindergarten through grade 12 and, in 2023-24, enrolled 7,165 students in eight schools.

sections.h2: Which North Bergen rental rules should a landlord check?
sections.html:
The township runs its own rent control program, and its office explains which apartments are covered, the legal base rent, capital improvement surcharges and annual registration. Files on residential properties are open for public inspection. The township's FAQ lists a yearly increase of 2.5 percent of base rent, allowed once in any twelve months, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants after approval.

Any renovation of an occupied or empty unit goes through the Rent Control office, with inspections before and after, and the application fee is $100. A landlord who will rent to a Section 8 tenant files a Certificate of Exemption, also $100. Ask the office whether your building is covered before you hand a buyer a rent roll.

Short-term rentals are tightly restricted. Ordinance 610-23, adopted September 20, 2023, bars them for anyone who had not registered a dwelling by September 6, 2023. Do not market a house on the strength of Airbnb income unless it already holds a registration certificate.

sections.h2: What does Code Enforcement look at before a North Bergen sale?
sections.html:
The township's Code Enforcement office inspects and issues residential and commercial certificates of occupancy, and it investigates illegal occupancy. The number is 201-392-2051. The township website also lists a Residential Owner Certificate form and an illegal apartment hotline, so ask whether any unit count in your deed differs from what is actually in the building.

If a mortgage goes into default, Ordinance 325-17 has the lender inspect the house and register it with the Building Department within 10 days, stating whether it is vacant or occupied. Owners facing default can ask that department how the registration works.

sections.h2: What do fees and forms look like at a North Bergen closing?
sections.html:
The state's realty transfer fee falls on the seller. A deed from an executor or administrator to an heir or devisee under a will or intestacy law is exempt, which matters for inherited houses, and so is a deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree. Prices above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee, 1% up to $2,000,000 and more above that.

A seller or heir who lives out of state prepays at least 2% of the deed price toward state income tax. The estimate is 10.75% of the gain when that comes out higher.

Hudson County deeds go to the Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages at 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, in Jersey City. Cashier and search hours run weekdays from 9:00 am to 2:00 pm, and phones are answered from 8:00 am to 3:45 pm at 201-395-4760. The Register also runs a free Recording Notification Service that warns owners when a document is filed against their property.

faqs.q: Is a North Bergen house with an unapproved apartment sellable?
faqs.a: A sale can go ahead, but tell buyers up front. The township's Code Enforcement office investigates illegal occupancy and keeps an illegal apartment hotline, so call 201-392-2051 and ask what a buyer or lender will need before closing.

Yes. The Rent Control office administers the ordinance, and its FAQ lists an annual increase of 2.5 percent of base rent, once in twelve months, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants. Covered rentals must register.

faqs.q: May a buyer turn my house into an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Generally no. Ordinance 610-23 ended new short-term rental registrations after September 6, 2023, and only dwellings holding a registration certificate by then are grandfathered. Confirm with the township before advertising it that way.

faqs.q: Is the transfer fee owed on an inherited house?
faqs.a: Not on the executor's deed that moves the house to an heir under the will or intestacy law. If the heir then sells to a buyer, that second deed is a sale and the fee applies to it.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for North Bergen property?
faqs.a: The Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, Jersey City. Your title company or attorney normally files it with the fee affidavit and the seller's residency form.
